parts.layout_phase: Period I (Mature Harappan); the structural phase within Period I is not stated in the sources we read
parts.what_was_built: The interim report of the first season states for Period I that 'the citadel mound was protected by a double fortification wall of stone rubble set in mud masonry', roughly squarish (93 m by 83 m), with a squarish watch tower at the south-western corner, an outer wall of large boulders and an inner wall of smaller stones; where the inner wall broadens and slopes and where a ramp joins the two walls on the east the excavators saw landing platforms (IAR 1987-88, p. 17). The second season reports 'a twin wall encircling the site' (IAR 1988-89, p. 11), and the third a gate 'with bastions' and a sloping ramp on the eastern part of the mound, without a period attribution in the summary (IAR 1989-90, p. 22).
parts.excavator_basis: The final report, which we know only through Kanungo and colleagues, gives Period I as 'layers 20-7, 2400-1900 BCE' (Dhavalikar et al. 1996: 27, quoted in kanungo2025bhagatrav p. 59), with radiocarbon dates of 2291 BC (PRL-1370, layer 12, structural phase B) and 2451-2356 BC (BS-567) from the middle of Period I (p. 41, quoted on kanungo2025bhagatrav pp. 59-61). The excavators' interim report had given Period I as 'c. 2300-1900 BC' without a stated basis (IAR 1987-88, p. 17), and the next season dated the whole settlement 'between circa 2200-1700 BC' 'on the basis of the artefacts' (IAR 1988-89, p. 11).

radiocarbon.context: layer 12, 'middle level of period I, which marks the structural phase B'
radiocarbon.note: Value taken from Kanungo and colleagues' Table 1, which cites Dhavalikar, Raval and Chitalwala 1996, Kuntasi: A Harappan Emporium on West Coast, p. 41; we could not obtain that report. The table prints '3820±170 BC' in the column headed 'Radiocarbon age (yr BP)' and does not state the half-life, so the 5568 fields are left empty. The calibrated figure is a single year as printed; the table footnote says calibrated dates are 'as in the original references and not recalculated'.

radiocarbon.calibrated_published: 2451-2356 BC; the Period I row adds 'Average 2451, 2433, 2392, 2384 and 2356 BC'
radiocarbon.note: Value taken from Kanungo and colleagues' Table 1, which cites Dhavalikar, Raval and Chitalwala 1996, Kuntasi: A Harappan Emporium on West Coast, p. 41; we could not obtain that report. No radiocarbon age is printed for this Birbal Sahni Institute sample.

syntheses.statement: Kanungo and colleagues place Kuntasi Period I as beginning 'from the end of the early Mature phase' and covering 'the entire late Mature Harappan phase', with Period II (layers 6-1, 1900-1700 BCE) Late Harappan, and count Kuntasi among Sorath Harappan settlements with fortifications that are not 'close to what we get in Classic Harappan sites'.

parts.conflicts: The excavators' own range for Period I moved from c. 2300-1900 BC (IAR 1987-88) to 2200-1700 BC for the whole settlement (IAR 1988-89) to 2400-1900 BCE in the final report as quoted by Kanungo and colleagues. The sources we read do not say in which part of Period I the fortification was built, so the radiocarbon dates from the middle of Period I bracket the occupation, not the wall.

first_occupation.basis: Period I spans layers 20-7, 2400-1900 BCE in the final report (Dhavalikar et al. 1996: 27, quoted in kanungo2025bhagatrav p. 59); an open pottery kiln was found 'in the earliest levels of Period I' (IAR 1987-88, p. 18). The interim report gave c. 2300-1900 BC (IAR 1987-88, p. 17).

notes: Kuntasi (Bibino Timbo), in Malia taluk in Rajkot district, was excavated by M. K. Dhavalikar, V. Shinde and S. Atre of Deccan College with M. H. Raval and Y. M. Chitalwala of the Gujarat State Department of Archaeology in seasons reported from 1987-88 to 1989-90. The final report, Dhavalikar, Raval and Chitalwala 1996, Kuntasi: A Harappan Emporium on West Coast (Deccan College), was not available to us: it is not on archive.org and we found only bookseller listings. We therefore rely on the three interim notes in Indian Archaeology: A Review and on the values Kanungo and colleagues quote from the final report. The fortification is assigned to Period I in the interim report, but we could not find which structural phase it belongs to. A third date, PRL-1371 (printed '3750±140 BC', calibrated 2145 BC, layer 5, Period II), is from the later period and is left out. Neither PRL-1370 nor PRL-1371 appears in the Physical Research Laboratory date lists in Radiocarbon, which end in 1991; no Bayesian model exists. Statements of wall direction in these sources were not recorded.
